A1.justification: Both PDFs describe TimeAlign and provide readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A-F. The expanded references and repagination in v4 do not create material comparison gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original forecasting experiments, ablations, plug-in comparisons, efficiency measurements, and supplementary stock-market and high-frequency analyses in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in Section 5 and Appendix E, including numerical benchmark comparisons and ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same prediction and reconstruction branches, projection and asymmetric gradient flow, local/global alignment objectives, adaptive weights, and joint loss. The reconstruction branch remains training-only.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the four ETT subsets, Weather, Electricity, Traffic, Solar, and the NASDAQ/NYSE stock datasets. Added citations concerning irregular forecasting, imputation, and anomaly detection do not introduce evaluated tasks or datasets.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main forecasting comparisons, iTransformer/DLinear plug-in experiments, and stock-market evaluation (Tables 1, 3, 6, 9, and 10). Newly cited methods such as CrossGNN, HDMixer, and FreDF are not added to these comparisons.

E3.justification: Forecasting horizons, stated look-back search ranges, dataset splits, model and training settings, and evaluation metrics remain unchanged. Citations appended to Appendices D.3 and E.1 do not revise the batch sizes or search settings.

E4.justification: The local/global ablations, reconstruction diagnostics, stock-market robustness tests, high-frequency analysis, and alignment-weight sensitivity study are retained unchanged. The distribution visualizations and supplementary forecasting examples also match.

E5.justification: Both specify three experimental runs and retain the same standard-deviation reporting in Table 7 and Wilcoxon test against TVNet, including p = 1.37e-8 and the reported 99% confidence level.

E6.justification: Reported scores, rankings, and plotted findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, TimeAlign's ETTm1 MSE/MAE remain 0.340/0.367 in Table 1, and its NASDAQ values remain 0.649/0.879 in Table 10.

T1.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B-C retain the same reconstruction-generalization argument, assumptions, and mutual-information derivations. The method equations and high-frequency error definition in Appendix E.7 are also unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same alignment paradigm, plug-and-play forecasting claims, frequency-preservation claims, and theoretical contributions concerning generalization and mutual information.

C2.justification: Interpretations of distribution alignment, spectral preservation, and robustness remain unchanged. Section 5.4 retains the explanations involving Weather/Solar outliers and zero-imputed values, while Appendix E.8 retains the qualification about excessive alignment weights.

D1.justification: Both provide the same PyTorch/Adam setup, NVIDIA V100 32GB hardware, learning rates, batch sizes, Table 5 hyperparameters, and code-access URL. Added citations disclose no additional implementation settings or access instructions.

R1.justification: v4 adds fourteen references, including HDMixer, CrossGNN, DBLoss, FreDF, and Time-o1, and removes Wu et al. (2020), replacing its GNN citation with Huang et al. (2023). These additions broaden citations within existing passages without substantially revising the positioning or novelty argument.

P1.justification: Citation insertions and a small rearrangement of citation placement in Section 2.2 modify local prose. The terminology, section order, explanatory narrative, and appendix organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: All nine figures and eleven tables retain their designs, labels, and captions. Local layout changes include shifting Table 5 and Figure 6 downward and changing how Appendix E prose flows around existing tables and figures.

improvement.justification: v4 broadens acknowledgment of prior work through additional citations, but adds no substantive comparative discussion. The method, mathematical arguments, complete empirical evidence, reproducibility details, and limitations remain unchanged. The modest prose and layout edits have little effect on readability, leaving overall paper quality essentially the same.
